deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 67-69). The previous page gives a criterion for a commutative square X ⊂ Y, p: X → Z, Z ⊂ S, p': Y → S to be a pushout S ≅ Y ⊔_X Z. The conditions are:
(a) Z → S is a mono;
(b) the square is cartesian, X = p'^{-1}(Z);
(c) Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∨ (X ×_Z X);
(d) Z ⊔ Y → S is an effective epi.
The aim of these 'topologie modérée' notes is to show that the class of tame spaces, those embeddable in some cube I^m, is stable under such gluings. That means realizing the pushout concretely inside some I^m by a map Y → I^m that restricts on X to a map factoring through Z (top-right diagram 'X ↪ Y, Z ↪ I^m comm').

This page treats the basic case Z = e, a point, i.e. collapsing a closed subspace X ⊂ Y to a point.

Step 1. Write X as a fibre X = φ^{-1}(e), with φ = (φ_1..φ_n): Y → I^n and e = (ε_1..ε_n). Choose an embedding ψ = (ψ_1..ψ_p): Y ↪ I^p.

Step 2, the key trick. Use the 'blow-down' map I×I → I×I, (x,y) ↦ (x, xy). It contracts the segment {0}×I to the point (0,0) and is injective off x = 0: from (x, xy) with x ≠ 0 one recovers y. The page checks this explicitly: (x,xy) = (x',x'y') gives x = x' and, if x ≠ 0, y = y'.

Step 3. Form χ_ij = (φ_i, φ_i ψ_j): Y → (I×I), i.e. the products f_i g_j. Together with φ this gives Y → (I×I)^{np} × I^n. The cases are:
- On X all φ_i = ε_i, which should be 0, so every χ_ij is constant: X goes to one point. The note 'χ_ij factorise par e_i × I ⊂ I×I' expresses this.
- Off X some φ_i ≠ 0, so all ψ_j, hence the point of Y, are recovered: the map is injective on Y − X.

Step 4. To verify condition (c), Grothendieck reduces to a universal model: Y' = I^{n+p} containing X' = I^p as the fibre over e, with Y ⊂ Y' via (φ, ψ) and X = Y ∩ X'. The same formula defines Y' → S'. Then Y ×_S Y = (Y×Y) ×_{Y'×Y'} (Y' ×_S Y'). Since Y → Y' is injective, Δ_{Y/Y'} = Δ_Y, giving Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∨ (X×X) from Y' ×_S Y' = Δ_{Y'} ∨ (X'×X'). A struck attempt 'Y ×_S Y = X ×_Y Y = Y' and a '≠' record a false start.

Step 5 (next page). The general Z is handled by combining an embedding of Z (pulled back via p) with functions g_{p+β} cutting out X, which reduces to this point case.

Upside-down and struck through on the sheet is a draft note: 'Dear Fujii Guruji, Please accept my most cordial wishes of welcome in France and of a very happy stay in Paris'. The sheet was reused scrap paper.
errors: The collapse via (x,y) ↦ (x,xy) only contracts ε_i × I to a point if ε_i = 0. The page writes general (ε_1..ε_n) and 'ε_i × I'; one must first translate so that e = 0 (or use |x − ε_i|). The marginal 'oy = 0' suggests he noticed this.

Injectivity off X plus condition (c) gives a bijection onto the image. Identifying the image with the quotient topology (condition (d), effective epi) needs compactness/properness, e.g. Y compact and X closed, or the tame analogue. This is not addressed on this page.
A struck false start, 'Y ×_S Y = X ×_Y Y = Y', marked '≠', is corrected by the base-change argument through Y' = I^{n+p}.

ideas.what: Criterion for a square to be a pushout (gluing along a closed subspace): mono, cartesian, Y ×_S Y = Δ_Y ∨ X ×_Z X, effective epi
ideas.modern_name: Gluing/pinching criterion for closed pushouts in a regular/extensive category (effective equivalence relation generated by X ×_Z X)
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore (topos theory / descent; cf. Johnstone, Elephant, on pushouts along monos)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 asks for tame theories stable under such quotients, without this formulation

ideas.what: Embedding the quotient Y/X in a cube using the blow-down map (x,y) ↦ (x,xy) applied to (φ_i, φ_i ψ_j)
ideas.modern_name: Embeddability of quotients/gluings of compact semialgebraic (o-minimal) sets; polynomial collapse map
ideas.usually_credited_to: Robson (embedding semialgebraic spaces, 1983); Delfs–Knebusch; Brumfiel (semialgebraic quotients, 1987); van den Dries (o-minimal quotients, 1998)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse mentions only the desideratum of stability of tame spaces under such constructions

ideas.what: Reduction of the fibre-product check to a universal model Y' = I^{n+p} ⊃ X' = I^p via base change
ideas.modern_name: Base change of the kernel pair along an embedding

missed.claim: A struck-through draft welcome note to 'Fujii Guruji', almost certainly Nichidatsu Fujii (founder of Nipponzan Myōhōji, called 'Guruji'), is written on this sheet. It ties the 'topologie modérée' notes in time to Grothendieck's contacts with that Buddhist order and to Fujii's visit to Paris.
missed.quote: Dear Fujii Guruji, Please accept my most cordial wishes of welcome in France and of a very happy stay in Paris
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Biographical dating: it fixes these tame-topology notes around Fujii's visit to France (c. 1974?). It also documents Grothendieck's direct correspondence with Fujii, which is less documented than his hosting of Nipponzan Myōhōji monks.

missed.claim: An early (1974) concrete attempt to prove that cube-embeddable tame spaces are stable under gluing along closed subspaces. This predates Robson/Brumfiel/van den Dries' semialgebraic and o-minimal quotient theorems, but uses only elementary techniques.
missed.quote: χ_ij factorise par e_i × I ⊂ I×I ; (x,y) ↦ (x,xy)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical precedence only; the results are now standard in o-minimal geometry.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is a correct but standard elementary construction (embedding a quotient by collapsing via (x,y) ↦ (x,xy)), later established in the semialgebraic/o-minimal literature. It is of interest mainly as an early concrete step of Grothendieck's tame-topology programme. The welcome note to Fujii Guruji is a small but genuine biographical datum.
transcription_corrections: 'Dear Fujii Gurugi' should read 'Dear Fujii Guruji' (Nichidatsu Fujii).
'Pan's' / 'Paris,' is 'Paris,', the end of the letter line '...happy stay in Paris'.
'xy = [-x-]y' [-x ≠ 0-]' reads as 'xy = x'y', x ≠ 0', concluding y = y'.
'∫ × ∫' denotes hooked embedding arrows (↪) Y → Y', not integrals.
The sheet number '68' is written upside down; the archive page is 66.
